FACTS OF THE CASE 1.
Briefly stated, the facts of the petition are that on 05.11.2021, at about 05:20 p.m., petitioner namely Arti was coming back to her house at C-19, Amar Colony, East Gokalpur, Delhi, from her office.

It has been alleged that when the petitioner reached near Ashok Nagar bus stand, the offending vehicle i.e. a motorcycle bearing registration no. DL-13SN-8368, suddenly came and hit the petitioner Arti with a great force.
It has been further alleged that the offending vehicle was being driven by its driver i.e. respondent no. 1 herein, at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without taking due caution.
It has been also alleged that due to the said accident, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained crush injuries on her right leg apart from other injuries and fracture all over the body.

Allegedly, the respondent no. 1 was caught hold of by the public persons at the spot of the accident and someone from the public made a call at 100 no., while the injured and R1 were taken to GTB hospital for primary treatment.
The injured petitioner was thereafter referred to RML hospital, Delhi for further treatment.
An FIR bearing no. 645/21, PS Jyoti Nagar for the offences u/s 279/337 IPC, also came to be registered against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Finally, the present claim petition/DAR came to be filed in due course on 28.02.2022.

WS / Reply of Respondents HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:

In its WS filed by respondent no. 1/2, being the driver cum owner of the offending vehicle, it has been contended that one another offending offending vehicle might have caused the accident and it might have ran away from the spot.
It has been further contended that the offending vehicle was duly insured with R3 i.e. ICICI Lombard Insurance Co. Ltd.
The respondent no. 1/2 denied the allegations against him and prayed for the dismissal of the DAR/claim petition.

3. During the course of proceedings, an application came to be moved on behalf of R3 i.e. insurance company, for deletion of its name from the array of parties as the offending vehicle was not insured on the date of the accident.
The said application was allowed by Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 31.10.2022, vide which R3 i.e. insurance company, stood deleted from the array of parties.

sentences.text: Issue wise findings Issue no.1

Whether petitioner Arti suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 05.11.2021 at about 05:20 pm near Footover Bridge, Ashok Nagar bus stand within the jurisdiction of PS Jyoti Nagar, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no.
DL13SN-8368 being driven by respondent no. 1/driver?
OPP 13.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court

HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.02.06 16:46:27 +0530 and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs Amir Chand &
Ors, 2011 (1) SCR 1906 (Civil Appeal No. 1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
14.

sentences.text: In the present case, the petitioner has examined herself as PW-1 to prove her contentions.

She has categorically stated in her examination on oath that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent act of respondent no. 1 as the latter was driving the offending vehicle in a very rash and negligent manner at a very high speed and that the offending vehicle had hit the petitioner with great force.
The said contentions are duly corroborated by the findings of the police as mentioned in the DAR and no ground has been made out by the respondent to disbelieve the same.

15. The very fact that R-1 has already been specifically arrayed as an accused in case FIR No. 645/21,
PS Jyoti Nagar, for the offences u/s 279/337 IPC is itself a strong circumstance to support the above said HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.02.06 16:46:37 +0530 testimony of PW-1 on these issues.

The copies of FIR,
Site plan, seizure memos, mechanical inspection report and charge sheet u/s 173 Cr.P.C also corroborate the oral testimony of PW-1.
16.

Furthermore, the position of law in this regard has been made clear in the case of "National Insurance Co., Vs Puspha Rana", 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, wherein it has been held that filing of Chargesheet is sufficient proof of the negligence and involvement of the offending vehicle.

Similar observations have been made in the case of "United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors.", 2014 (2) Tac 846 Del, that if the claimant was able to prove the criminal case on record pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle, whereby the criminal records showing Dar - Arti vs Rashid Malik on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81078877/
5 completion of investigation by the police and filing of Chargesheet under Section 279/337 IPC against the driver have been proved, then, the documents mentioned above are sufficient to establish the fact that the driver was negligent in causing the accident.
17.

sentences.text:
Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of R-1,
if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending motorcycle) hit the injured Arti.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased or any other such person, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.02.06 16:46:52 +0530 time.

In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time leading to the injuries to the injured Arti.
18. In view of the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the injuries to the petitioner Arti in the above accident.
19. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the injured Arti suffered injuries on account of neglect and default of R1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
The issue at hand is thus decided against the respondent and in favour of the petitioner.
Issue no. (ii) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
OPP 20.

On the basis of findings upon issue no. (i), it is clear that the incident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and injuries had been caused to the petitioner in the incident.
Hence, petitioner is entitled to compensation in this case.
21. The issue at hand is accordingly decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondent.
LIABILITY 22.
Now the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Herein, it is pertinent to note that the R3 i.e. insurance company already stood deleted from array of parties vide HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.02.06 16:47:00 +0530 order 31.10.2022 as the offending vehicle was not insured at the time of accident.

Hence, on the basis of entire above stated facts and circumstances and discussion of evidence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that respondent no.1 being driver cum owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the entire compensation to the petitioner.

sentences.text: At this stage, while the Tribunal was pronouncing its judgment at the final stage, all the parties submitted that they have amicably settled the quantum of compensation to be paid by R1 i.e. driver cum owner to the petitioner for an amount of Rs. 2,25,000/-.
It has been agreed between the parties that out of the said amount, Rs. 1,00,000/- shall be paid by R1 on 01.03.2025 and remaining amount of Rs. 1,25,000/- shall be paid on 30.06.2025 through DD.
Separate statement of the petitioner and the R1 also recorded to this effect.

The Tribunal is satisfied that the aforesaid settlement regarding quantum of compensation payable in this case has been arrived between the parties voluntarily and without any force, fear or coercion.

Hence, in order to finally put the matter to rest and to give it a complete finality, the aforesaid amount of Rs. 2,25,000/- is hereby awarded as full and final compensation to be granted in favour of the petitioner in this case by the respondent no. 1/ 2.
ISSUE NO.3 / RELIEF 24.

In view of the findings on the aforesaid issues, the petitioner is hereby awarded a sum of Rs.2,25,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh Twenty Five Thousand only) to be payable by respondent no. 1 in UCO Bank, HARUN by HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date: 2025.02.06 16:47:12 +0530 Karkardooma Court Branch, Delhi bearing account no. 20780110171912; IFSC: UCBA0002078.

It is further to be noted that the settlement with the respondent also includes the settlement of the criminal case pertaining to the incident in question bearing FIR No. 645/21, PS Jyoti Nagar, for which petitioner will give her statement before concerned criminal court without seeking any further compensation.
RELEASE/APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION TO THE PETITIONER 25.
Finally, in view of the statements of the parties, an award in the sum of Rs. 2,25,000/- has been passed towards full and final compensation amount of the present DAR/claim petition.

Out of the above said amount, Rs. 1,00,000/- shall be paid by R1 on 01.03.2025 and remaining amount of Rs.
1,25,000/- shall be paid on 30.06.2025 through DD.

Manager, UCO Bank is directed to release the said amount in the savings account of the petitioner as and when it gets deposited by R1.
26.
Copy of the Award be given to the parties free of costs.
Copy of this Award be also sent to concerned court of Ld. JMFC and DLSA.
27. File be consigned to Record Room as per rules.

Hence, in order to finally put the matter to rest and to give it a complete finality, the aforesaid amount of Rs. 2,25,000/- is hereby awarded as full and final compensation to be granted in favour of the petitioner in this case by the respondent no. 1/ 2.
